q: In the payments-api project, what is adr-capture-outbox?
a: The design behind asynchronous capture (accepted 2026-08-20): the request transaction inserts a row in payments.capture_outbox next to the ledger row; capture-worker polls every 500 ms in batches of 200 and calls acquirer-gateway; the capture_async flag selects the path per merchant. Targets: POST /payments p95 under 200 ms, capture lag p95 under 2 s. Kafka and a direct async task were rejected.

q: What do we know about lib-retry-v2 in payments-api?
a: The current retry library (PR #418, 2026-08-04): exponential backoff of 200 ms base with full jitter, capped at 2 s, three attempts in total, no retry on 4xx, Retry-After honoured. It replaced lib-retry-v1 after the fixed 500 ms delay synchronised retries on 2026-07-30. 9 test cases in tests/test_retry.py. Owner Priya Nair.

q: What is the auth success rate metric in payments-api and what is its current value?
a: Approved authorisations over attempts minus fraud declines, per day, from payments.ledger. 94.1% in the first half of September 2026 (n = 1.9M attempts); the agreed floor is 93%.

q: What does req-idempotent-retries require in the payments-api project?
a: Every POST /payments must be safe to retry for at least 24 hours: a retried request with the same Idempotency-Key never charges twice (merchant contracts, clause 4.3). Acceptance: a replay of 10,000 duplicate requests produces 0 extra charges. Owner Lena Fischer.

q: What is risk-redis-single-az about in payments-api?
a: redis-payments runs in one availability zone and a failover loses the last second of writes, so a retried request in that window is not recognised and can be charged twice. About one failover per quarter (2 in 2025). Owner Dan Okafor; the proposed mitigation was keys in Postgres.

q: What came of bug-double-charge in payments-api?
a: The fix PR #412 moved the idempotency check into the ledger transaction (14 new tests, a 10,000-request replay with 0 double charges), the ADR adr-idempotency-v2 moved the keys to Postgres with a 7-day TTL, and both shipped in release v3.4.0 on 2026-08-05.

q: What came of the incident inc-2026-08-11-ledger-lag in payments-api?
a: The decision dec-capture-async (2026-08-14) moved capture off the request path, and the plan plan-postgres-16-migration (2026-09-15) moves payments-db from Postgres 13 to 16 by 2026-11-30 because the failovers took 39 minutes.

q: What was decided about q-capture-mode in payments-api?
a: First dec-capture-sync (2026-04-02): capture synchronously in the request path. It was overturned by dec-capture-async (2026-08-14) after the 2026-08-11 incident: capture runs after the response through a worker, authorisation stays synchronous.

q: What led to lib-retry-v2 in payments-api?
a: The finding fnd-retry-amplification: fixed 500 ms retries from lib-retry-v1 amplified load 2.4 times for nine minutes on 2026-07-30 and raised acquirer-gateway timeouts from 0.3% to 7.9%. lib-retry-v2 (PR #418) supersedes lib-retry-v1.

q: What is adr-idempotency-v3 built on in payments-api?
a: It supersedes adr-idempotency-v2 (keys in Postgres, 7 days), which came from bug-double-charge and superseded adr-idempotency-v1 (keys in Redis, 24 hours). v3 keeps keys 30 days and binds them to a body hash; it shipped in rel-v3-5-0.

q: What does payments-api call, read and write?
a: Calls orders-service (order lookup), risk-service (fraud score) and acquirer-gateway (authorisation); reads customers.cards; writes payments.ledger through ledger-writer and payments.capture_outbox for capture-worker.

q: Who owns payments-api and who is on call for it?
a: Owned by platform-team; on-call Dan Okafor. Repo git/payments-api, entrypoint src/payments/app.py.

q: What does capture-worker read and call in payments-api?
a: It reads payments.capture_outbox, calls acquirer-gateway through lib-retry-v2 and marks the ledger row captured; 3 replicas in prod-eu, owned by platform-team.

q: What writes payments.ledger and what reads it?
a: ledger-writer (src/payments/ledger.py) writes one row per attempt keyed by request_id inside the request transaction, used by payments-api; the finance export job jobs/ledger_export reads it. Owned by platform-team.

q: Which clients still use the gRPC endpoint of payments-api, and until when?
a: orders-service and reporting-batch, 3.2% of traffic in 2026-08. The endpoint is retired on 2026-12-15; orders-team migrates by 2026-11-20.

q: Does payments-api capture synchronously or asynchronously now?
a: Asynchronously: since dec-capture-async (2026-08-14) capture runs after the response through capture-worker and the outbox, under the capture_async flag, which reached 100% of merchants with release v3.5.0. The earlier dec-capture-sync (synchronous capture) is superseded.

q: How long are idempotency keys kept now in payments-api, and where?
a: 30 days, in the Postgres table payments.idempotency_keys, bound to a SHA-256 of the body (adr-idempotency-v3, accepted 2026-09-22, shipped in v3.5.0). The 7-day rule of adr-idempotency-v2 is superseded.

q: What is the current retry policy for outbound calls in payments-api?
a: lib-retry-v2: three attempts, exponential backoff with a 200 ms base and full jitter, capped at 2 s, no retries on 4xx, Retry-After honoured. lib-retry-v1 (two attempts, fixed 500 ms) is superseded.

q: Where do idempotency keys live now in payments-api, Redis or Postgres?
a: Postgres: payments.idempotency_keys, written in the same transaction as the ledger row, with Redis as a read-through cache only (since adr-idempotency-v2, 2026-08-03; refined by adr-idempotency-v3). The Redis-only store of adr-idempotency-v1 is superseded.

q: What is the current release of payments-api in prod-eu and what did it ship?
a: v3.5.0, deployed 2026-09-25: asynchronous capture at 100% of merchants (PR #431) and 30-day idempotency keys with a body hash (PR #437); 1,842 tests green in 11 minutes.

q: What are the p95 latency, peak load and error rate of POST /payments after v3.5.0?
a: p95 160 ms and p99 410 ms, peak 1,250 req/s, error rate 0.21%, measured in prod-eu from 2026-09-26 to 2026-09-28.

q: How many duplicate captures happened on 2026-07-30 in payments-api, and how much was refunded?
a: 143 duplicate captures; 61,400 EUR refunded the same day. The failover window was 09:12 to 09:21 CET.

q: How many tests ran in CI for payments-api release v3.5.0 and how long did CI take?
a: 1,842 tests green in 11 minutes (v3.4.0 had 1,796 tests in 9 minutes).

q: What are the capture lag p95 and p99 of capture-worker, and when does it page?
a: p95 1.4 s and p99 3.2 s over 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-24; the alert capture-lag-high pages at 10 s p95 for 5 minutes.

q: How much of the 290 ms p95 of POST /payments was the risk-service call, in June 2026?
a: 180 ms of 290 ms; acquirer-gateway 70 ms and the ledger write 12 ms. The 300 ms budget was missed on 2 of 14 days; a 60 s risk cache would save about 110 ms.

q: Why did capture move off the request path in payments-api?
a: Because the 2026-08-11 payments-db failover held 2,310 captures inside requests for 39 minutes and 318 timed out at the gateway (error rate peak 3.8%); dec-capture-async moved capture to a worker after the response.

q: Why were idempotency keys moved from Redis to Postgres in payments-api?
a: Because a redis-payments failover on 2026-07-30 lost the keys of the previous second and 143 retried requests were charged twice (61,400 EUR refunded); the keys now live in payments.idempotency_keys in the same transaction as the ledger row, at a cost of +1.7 ms p50.

q: Why is the idempotency key TTL 30 days instead of 7 in payments-api?
a: Because 41 merchants replay month-end batches (fin-replays, 2026-09-15); keys are kept 30 days and bound to a body hash, at about 2.1 GB of table growth per 30 days.

q: Why was lib-retry-v1 replaced in payments-api?
a: Its fixed 500 ms delay synchronised client retries during the 2026-07-30 failover: acquirer-gateway saw 2.4 times its normal load for nine minutes and timeouts rose from 0.3% to 7.9%. Jittered exponential backoff (lib-retry-v2) fixed it.

q: Why is payments-db moving to Postgres 16?
a: Because the 2026-08-11 failovers took 39 minutes on Postgres 13, while 16 fails over in under 60 seconds in the vendor test; the migration runs in three steps by 2026-11-30.
